title: Repurposing Diffusion-Based Image Generators for Monocular Depth Estimation
layout_note: Three stacked input rows (image x, depth d, sampled timestep and noise) run left to right; the image latent and the noised depth latent converge on one concat circle before the U-Net at top right, and the training objective sits in a large pale-yellow box at bottom right.
grouping: No frames around the pipeline; the three input rows are stacked and converge on a concat node and the U-Net at top right; only the training objective has a container, a pale-yellow rounded box at bottom right.
shapes_depth: Inputs are a real interior photo and its colour-mapped depth drawn as thick 3D slabs; latents and noise are small 3D cubes with a coloured mosaic face; encoders are pink trapezoids with a padlock icon; operations (Add Noise, Sample Noise) light-blue rounded squares; the U-Net a light-blue bow-tie shape; concat a white circle with a bold outline; timestep t a grey rounded tag; the objective box shows epsilon and epsilon-hat as two small noise thumbnails inside a squared norm.
proposed_highlight: The trainable U-Net is the only blue shape that is not a fixed noise operation and carries no padlock, while the frozen encoders are pink with padlocks; the objective is the largest coloured box (pale yellow). The concatenation that conditions on the image is a small white circle.
lesson: Draw the loss as its own terms - the sampled noise thumbnail and the predicted one inside the norm - fed by straight lines from where each is made, so the objective visibly compares two drawn representations.
notes: venue: unverified (the PDF carries no venue line); remembered as CVPR 2024. year = arXiv preprint year. Method name Marigold from the caption. Fig. 3 of the paper draws the matching inference scheme (iterative denoising inside a green panel).

arrangement.units: one unframed diagram of three converging input rows; the objective alone sits in a pale-yellow rounded box
arrangement.inputs_as: a real RGB image slab and a colour-mapped depth slab, plus a grey 't ~ U(T)' tag on the bottom row
arrangement.losses_at: bottom right: below the U-Net output epsilon-hat and at the end of the sampled-noise line running along the bottom
arrangement.shared: the frozen latent encoder is drawn twice, once per input row, both pink with padlocks

taxonomy.task: monocular depth estimation by fine-tuning a pretrained latent diffusion model

insights.structure: Three stacked input rows (image, depth, timestep) run left to right; the depth latent is noised and joins the image latent at a concat node, the U-Net predicts epsilon-hat, and the objective box at bottom right takes epsilon-hat from above and epsilon from the bottom row.
insights.data: Image and depth are real slabs, every latent and noise tensor is a textured cube (z^(x), z^(d), z_t^(d), epsilon, epsilon-hat), and the objective repeats the epsilon and epsilon-hat thumbnails inside its norm.
insights.emphasis: Padlocks and pink fill mark the frozen encoders, leaving the blue U-Net as the trained part; the pale-yellow objective is the largest coloured box.
insights.flow: Thin black orthogonal arrows, mostly straight left to right; t enters Add Noise and the U-Net as short vertical side tags; epsilon runs along the bottom to the objective with one branch up into Add Noise.
insights.avoid: Blue fills both the trained U-Net and the parameter-free Add Noise / Sample Noise steps, so colour does not separate learned from fixed operations; the concat node - the method's conditioning - is the smallest element.

core.what: the image latent z^(x) from the top row and the noised depth latent z_t^(d) from the middle row converge on one white 'concat' circle that feeds the U-Net

relations.form: each input row runs left to right: input slab -> padlocked pink encoder -> textured latent cube; the depth row continues through Add Noise to z_t^(d)
the frozen latent encoder appears twice as identical pink padlocked trapezoids stacked in one column, one per input row
epsilon from the bottom row and epsilon-hat from the U-Net meet in the objective box, drawn as two noise thumbnails inside ||. - .||^2
the timestep t enters Add Noise and the U-Net as grey tags on short vertical arrows from above and below

channels.colour: pink = frozen VAE encoder; light blue = operations, both the trained U-Net and the fixed Add Noise / Sample Noise (blue carries two meanings; the padlock separates frozen from trained only on the encoders); pale yellow = training objective; grey = scalar inputs (t); mosaic textures = latents and noise
channels.shape: trapezoid = encoder, bow-tie = U-Net, rounded square = operation, circle = concat, cube = latent or noise tensor, slab = input image / depth, padlock icon = frozen
channels.line: one style: thin black arrows; t enters through short vertical arrows
channels.frame: only the objective has a container (pale-yellow rounded box)

quality.strengths: Every representation is drawn as a textured cube between its maker and its consumer, and the loss shows epsilon and epsilon-hat themselves rather than a formula in a box; frozen vs trained is marked by padlock icons on the encoders; image conditioning by concatenation is visible as two rows converging on one node; arrows are short and orthogonal.
quality.weaknesses: Blue fill is shared by the trained U-Net and the fixed noise operations; the concat node (the method's conditioning) is the smallest element while the generic objective box is the largest; t is drawn twice as separate tags; no line style separates the training-only path.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
